My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for three generations. I know this soil. I know the weather here. I have done wheat and corn my whole life and I will do it again this year — there is no reason to change what works.

I have about 8 mu of contracted land. All of it goes into the wheat-corn rotation, same as always. Wheat in autumn, corn after harvest. I do not have the strength anymore to manage anything more complicated — cotton is too much work for my back, and vegetables need someone watching them every day.

For wheat, I will buy improved seed from the village supply co-op, probably Jimai 22 or whatever they have that is certified. I stopped using old seed years ago because the yield is just worse. I do rotary tillage before planting — I rent the machine from the village cooperative, costs me a few hundred yuan. I water three times: once before the ground freezes, once at jointing, once at grain filling. I apply compound fertilizer as the base and urea at jointing. I spray herbicide in early spring and something for rust and aphids before harvest. I expect around 450 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant corn immediately. Hybrid seed — everyone uses hybrid now. I do rotary again, mix in fertilizer, and plant. Summer rains help so I only irrigate twice — once if it gets dry in July and once at silking if needed. I spray once for stem borer. Should get 550 jin per mu.

I am 70 years old. I use mechanized services for heavy tillage and harvest. My son helps during busy season. I keep costs low and stick to what I know.
